Giv is a character from the Shahnameh, the epic poem written by the Persian poet Ferdowsi in the 11th century. The Shahnameh recounts the history of Persia (modern-day Iran) from the creation of the world until the Islamic conquest of Persia in the 7th century.

In the Shahnameh, Giv is a renowned Iranian warrior and a close companion of the heroic king Kaveh the Blacksmith. Giv plays an important role in several key events and battles described in the epic.

Some key details about Giv from the Shahnameh:

- Giv is the son of Gudarz, another renowned Iranian hero and commander.

- He is known for his bravery, loyalty, and skill in battle. Giv is considered one of the greatest warriors fighting for the Iranian cause against foreign invaders.

- Giv accompanies the young prince Kai Khosrow when he flees the treacherous Turanian ruler Afrasiyab. Giv helps Kai Khosrow make his way safely back to Iran.

- Giv also plays a crucial role in the final battle between the Iranians and the Turanians, helping to secure victory for the Iranian forces.

- In the later parts of the Shahnameh, Giv continues to serve as a trusted general and advisor to the Iranian kings.

The character of Giv is seen as embodying the ideals of Iranian heroism, honor and devotion to the homeland in the Shahnameh. He is remembered as one of the most valiant and loyal warriors among the Iranian heroes of the epic.
